newsitem.title: UK: LME copper option vols steady before declaration.
newsitem.headline: LME copper option vols steady before declaration.

text.p: LME copper option volatilities consolidated this week ahead of next week's declaration which was not expected to spark much excitement, traders said.
Only if underlying futures prices shot up again, pushing the June contract towards a distant $2,700, would any fireworks be seen, they added.
Many players stood back this week after a bout of upside buying the previous week attributed to a Korean firm pushed up implied volatilities.
The buying of $2,600 and $2,700 call options had helped the futures market stay charged up, hitting fresh one-year highs.
"The buying of those calls made people nervous about the upside," a trader said.

The market saw hefty turnover on Wednesday, but like several times recently open interest data indicated that this was a crossing of positions or a give-up. LME data showed a turnover of 44,188 lots but open interest only increased by 3,917 lots.
Some further business was seen in upside strikes from $2,550 to $2,700 for 1997 dates, but the main feature was interest in downside material such as $2,100 and $2,200 for next year.
"There's been some producer interest," one trader said.
Some players took advantage of the firmer vols to do some granting, another said.
Implied at-the-money (ATM) volatility stabilised after last week's gains, with July bid at 20.0 percent, August at 18.5 percent and fourth quarter at 16.0 percent.
"In August, there was a good volume of business done at 19.0 percent," a trader said.
The options declaration next Wednesday was not expected to provide much excitement.
"Only if June moves up to $2,700, then we would run into quite a few shorts," a trader said. June was indicated on Friday morning around $2,600.
Aluminium saw some buying by players taking advantage of the weaker volatility, but it was not enough to push them higher.
Some $1,700 and further upside calls were picked up by speculators, one dealer said.
Another said granting had been seen of average 1998 at volatility as low as 14 percent.
Vols were little changed, with July bid at 15.0 percent, August at 15.25 percent and fourth quarter at 14.75 percent.
Business in most of the other metals was muted, but there was some two-way business in nickel and vols were down by about one half a point.
